title: Tenant authentication parity and source-bound Support Ticket admin contracts

phases.objective: Restore tenant user-JWT parity and compose exact source-bound OpenAPI path items for the fifteen uncovered Support Ticket admin lifecycle routes without weakening runtime authority gates.

e2e_journeys.actor: tenant member, platform administrator, backend operator, and governed OpenAPI maintenance
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The precise-contract registry reads Support Ticket runtime route ownership and split OpenAPI path items.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: All four tenant operations resolve userJwtAuth, all fifteen previously uncovered admin operations resolve exact reviewed path-item references, the root OpenAPI composes those references, and the missing-route gate returns zero uncovered Support Ticket routes.
steps: Require userJwtAuth on create, list, detail, and customer-event Support Ticket operations.
Bind every uncovered admin signature to routes/supportTicketRoutes.js and one exact split path-item reference.
Validate adminBearerAuth and backendApiKeyAuth on all admin operations.
Retain request and response envelopes that declare secrets_included=false while leaving operation-specific runtime validation authoritative.
Run precise registry composition before the missing-route coverage gate.
Regenerate bounded root OpenAPI and frontend dispatch/runtime-route evidence.
Reject generic TODO stubs, public admin security, unbound route ownership, or an uncovered support-ticket signature.
assertions: Exactly fifteen new admin route signatures are registered.
Every signature exists in routes/supportTicketRoutes.js with normalized ticket_id path syntax.
Every registry entry is source-bound to routes/supportTicketRoutes.js.
Brand-reference and remediation operations use support-ticket-admin-brand.yaml.
Diagnostics, execution, lifecycle, assignment, and event operations use support-ticket-admin-execution.yaml.
Shared request, response, parameter, error, no-secret, and no-provider evidence lives in support-ticket-admin-common.yaml.
All four tenant operations declare userJwtAuth and no tenant operation is public.
All admin operations declare adminBearerAuth or backendApiKeyAuth and no admin operation is public.
The generated-artifact evaluator reports missing_count=0 after precise registry composition.
No migration, SQL/database mutation, runtime authorization change, provider call, credential access, external send, deployment, Production mutation, protected-branch bypass, or force push occurs.

phases.objective: Exercise authenticated tenant reads and admin lifecycle operations against a non-production fixture while verifying typed failures and sanitized readback.
Reject stale approvals, missing trusted references, invalid transitions, cross-tenant ticket identifiers, absent credentials, and malformed evidence without leaking secrets.
This OpenAPI contract repair performs no provider or deployment canary.
No runtime, database, migration, provider, credential, external-send, deployment, or direct Production authority is granted.
